en.p: As shown in the figure, there is a semicircle with diameter AB, a segment of length 2. Take two points P, Q on arc AB so that $\angle\mathrm{PAB}=\theta$ and $\angle\mathrm{QBA}=2\theta$, and let R be the intersection of the two segments AP and BQ. Take a point S on segment AB, a point T on segment BR, and a point U on segment AR so that segment UT is parallel to segment AB and triangle STU is equilateral.

Let $f(\theta)$ be the area of the region enclosed by the two segments AR, QR and the arc AQ, and $g(\theta)$ the area of triangle STU. When $\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to 0+}\frac{g(\theta)}{\theta\times f(\theta)}=\frac{q}{p}\sqrt{3}$, find the value of $p+q$. (Here $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, and $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime natural numbers.) [4 points]
